claim: Bayer and McCreight's classic multiway balanced index appeared in a 1970 workshop and a 1972 Acta Informatica paper; paper is on B-trees, not every later B+ tree variant.
notes: 1970 conference version DOI 10.1145/1734663.1734671. Avoid attributing linked leaves to the original B-tree paper.

claim: B+ trees use linked leaves with full searchable entries at leaves; internal nodes retain routing copies, improving range traversal.
notes: Brown's teaching variant. Real engines have differing separator/fence key representations.

claim: On a B+ leaf split, the right leaf's separator key is copied into the parent while the key remains at leaf level.
notes: Explained for the min-right-child separator convention used by the toy algorithm.

claim: PostgreSQL B-Tree index pages form doubly linked levels and page splitting may cascade through parent pages and create new root.
notes: Implementation terminology says B-Tree; does not claim direct correspondence to every didactic invariant.

claim: PostgreSQL MVCC version churn and deduplication affect physical leaf index contents.
notes: A tuple points to a table row; duplicate keys can be represented as posting lists.

claim: Leading equality constraints are generally most useful for PostgreSQL multicolumn B-Tree indexes.
notes: Avoid universal claims about query planners and index-only scans.

claim: SQLite distinguishes table B-trees and index B-trees with different leaf and interior cell formats.
locator: B-tree Pages section and page cell formats
notes: Counterexample to unqualified assertions about physical row placement.

claim: For max internal children C=4 and leaf capacity L=3, inserting 35 into [20,25,30] splits into [20,25] and [30,35], copying 30 to the parent.
locator: Independent worked example following B+ split algorithm
notes: Arithmetic/invariant demonstration only; not a database benchmark.

claim: With root [20,30,40], inserting 37 and 38 induces leaf split at 37 and root separator overflow, yielding root [37].
locator: Independent worked example and Python tests
notes: The internal split promotes 37; the leaf retains 37.

claim: Point lookup uses O(log_F N) pages; a dense ordered range scan has an indicative O(log_F N + K/L) page cost under stated assumptions.
locator: Page-oriented B+ tree structure; asymptotic derivation from fanout and leaf chain
notes: Not a wall-clock benchmark; ignores heap fetch, cache, fragmentation, and I/O concurrency.
